area: Tenant health, readiness tenant checks, API call diagnostics and ZDX probes fitted to the tier: tenant_health.py, readiness.py, api_calls.py (hooked in zia_rate.attach, zia_rate.wait and the SDK's RequestExecutor and HTTPClient), ops_zdx.py, the HLT assessment checks, /report/health, Advanced settings and the Bulk changes result
title: Wave 7 gaps from the tool comparison closed: pending activation and SSL rule order in readiness, tenant health with certificate expiry thresholds, a bounded secret-free API call log, and tier-fitted ZDX probes with verified and assumed parts said apart

checks.what: ZIA activation status (zia.activate.status, GET /zia/api/v1/status, verified in SDK 1.11.3) read for any ZIA scope; PENDING and INPROGRESS are a readiness check needing attention with plain steps; a refused read is 'unknown'

SSL inspection rule order (zia.ssl_inspection_rules.list_rules, read only with DLP or ZIA platform ticked): a broad Do Not Inspect rule above Inspect rules, a broad Inspect rule above the exemptions, nothing inspecting what reaches the Default rule; disabled and scoped rules never shadow

Certificate expiry thresholds at the boundary seconds (expired at now, critical within 7 days inclusive, warning within 30 inclusive), custom thresholds, missing, boolean, NaN and unreadable dates, seconds, milliseconds and ISO 8601
Tenant health keeps only names, dates and states: an enrollment certificate's PEM and encrypted key in the read never reach the result
Scope rule: tenant health and the readiness checks read only what is ticked; out of scope or a bad threshold is a 400 before sign-in
API calls ring buffer bounded (DLP_CHECK_API_CALLS_MAX clamped to 50..20000), oldest dropped first and counted
API call rows hold no header, body, query, host, user info, id, email or secret: secret canaries over the real SDK and the echoing transport, in the list, the CSV and the JSON
ZDX payload oracle per tier (interval, CloudPath probe, predefined apps) and the verified /zdx/v1 prefix against the installed SDK; the configuration paths stay assumed

findings.title: Readiness did not say when ZIA changes were saved but not activated, although a deploy from this app ends with an activation that makes every pending change live, someone else's too
findings.fix: readiness.read reads zia.activate.status() for any ZIA scope; tenant_health.readiness_checks turns PENDING into a check with steps, shown on Start and /permissions

findings.title: Readiness and tenant health did not call out an SSL inspection rule order that keeps rules from applying (a broad Do Not Inspect rule above Inspect rules, an Inspect-all rule above the exemptions)
findings.fix: tenant_health.ssl_order, with plain steps naming the rules; read only when DLP or ZIA platform is ticked

findings.title: No warning before a ZIA SSL inspection intermediate CA certificate or a ZPA enrollment, web server or client signing certificate expired
findings.fix: tenant_health certificate items with warning and critical thresholds (30/7 days, settable), on /report/health and as assessment checks HLT.2 and HLT.3

findings.title: App Connector groups with no connector were not reported
No view of the Zscaler API calls the app made (status, timing, retries, rate-limit waits) to diagnose a failed or slow run
findings.fix: api_calls.py: a bounded in-memory log hooked at the paced session and the SDK executor, secret-free, per run, with CSV and JSON export (Advanced settings)

findings.title: ZDX probe setup used one interval for every customer, whatever the protection tier chosen
findings.fix: ops_zdx.TIERS (strict, balanced, permissive, healthcare): apps, interval and CloudPath per tier; looser choices are preview warnings

findings.title: The ZDX configuration API paths, bodies, intervals and step order cannot be verified: zscaler-sdk-python 1.11.3 has no ZDX configuration service
findings.reason: Nothing to verify against without a live tenant; the /zdx/v1 prefix, routing and body handling are verified, the rest stays marked ASSUMED in ops_zdx.py and on the page, and a test fails when the SDK gains the service

notes: Zscaler semantics implemented and their sources: activation status words ACTIVE, PENDING, INPROGRESS (the SDK model keeps status as free text: assumed); SSL inspection rules are evaluated in ascending order, first match wins, the Default rule last (ZIA SSL Inspection Leading Practices Guide, as the existing check 4.3 reads it); certExpDate (zia/models/intermediate_certificates.py, unit assumed epoch seconds, milliseconds recognised by size); validToInEpochSec (zpa/models/enrollment_certificates.py, certificates.py); singningCertExpiryInEpochSec (zpa/models/client_settings.py, the SDK's spelling); connectors and enrollmentCertId on App Connector groups and enrollmentCert.name on service edges (zpa/models).

The new-marks browser test hard-coded the 2026-10-28 features; adding the 2026-10-31 release pushes them out, so it now follows the manifest (the newest release's mark on Advanced settings, the narrow tour over the pages that still have marks).
Retries a caller sends itself (the assessment client after a 429) are folded into the earlier row by thread, method, path and a retryable answer within 15 minutes: a heuristic, said in api_calls.py.
Worker threads of a job (the assessment's fan-out) do not carry the job id, so their calls show without a run; builder runs do.
